findings.title: Example makes a staging principal the production fallback
findings.description: The primary example defines top-level ADMIN and DAILY_CAP values for staging while separately defining safer production values, even though the page says top-level values are conventionally the production truth used by a bare bounded deploy. The current CLI only rejects a bare deployment when a function has an explicit environment allowlist. For policies like this example, it strips the environments block, uses the top-level staging constants, and deploys to the app selected by project configuration. A later bare deployment targeting production would therefore grant the staging principal the production-wide read role and replace the production cap of 5000 with 50. A lower-trust staging identity could gain access to protected production data, while the cap change could also disrupt production behavior.
findings.recommendation: Make the top-level policy values the actual production defaults and place staging values only in the staging overlay. In the owning CLI, fail closed whenever a policy containing environments is deployed without an explicit environment, unless the user supplies a separate explicit option acknowledging deployment of the base policy.

revalidation.reasoning: The primary example places the staging administrator and cap in the top-level `constants`, while the production overlay contains a different administrator and a cap of 5000. The same page states that top-level values are the default and, by convention, the production truth used by a bare deployment. In the current CLI, environment overlay resolution only runs when `--environment` is supplied. Its environment-blind refusal checks only functions that have their own explicit environment allowlists, so this policy, which has no such functions, is admitted. The CLI then removes the entire `environments` block and resolves the target app from the explicit flag or authoritative `bounded.json` project configuration. Compile-time `@const.ADMIN` expansion therefore installs the staging identity into the broad admin read role, and `@const.DAILY_CAP` becomes 50 rather than the production value of 5000. A developer or CI job issuing the documented bare command while configured for production would grant the lower-trust staging principal production-wide reads and replace the intended production cap. The current CLI history still contains this exact behavior after the environment-overlay changes, and the false-positive register identifies no external deployment guard that would prevent the scenario.
